title: How to start a business: Zach Yadegari's fundamentals from building Cal AI
summary: Zach Yadegari (Cal AI founder, 19) lays out the basics of building a profitable business: product, selling, LTV vs CAC, scalability, delegating to employees with aligned incentives, and a bias toward speed. He also covers hiring, pricing via A/B testing, idea generation, co-founders and the mindset needed to absorb constant setbacks.

principles.text: A business is a product plus selling it; to be profitable, LTV must exceed CAC plus cost of goods.
principles.quote: your LTV needs to be greater than the CAC plus the cost of the good.

principles.text: Make both the product and the marketing channel scalable, not just profitable.
principles.quote: you want to make sure that your product is scalable. It's profitable. That's good, but it needs to be scalable.

principles.text: Hire people smarter than you with initiative, and use interviews to scare off non-grinders.
principles.quote: You also always want to hire people smarter than you.

principles.text: Align incentives with equity or KPI-tied bonuses so employees care; you can't really overpay great talent.
principles.quote: I would very strongly recommend that you should have something that aligns incentives. If it's not bonuses, then equity.

principles.text: Move fast with a bias toward action; ideas are worthless without execution.
principles.quote: Execution is everything. Ideas are worthless.

principles.text: Only traffic, conversion rate and retention/LTV matter; double down on what already works and A/B test everything.
principles.quote: If they double down on that, which now they are, it's like, okay, let's focus on paid ads.
